'''Edna Schechtman''' ({{Langx|he|עדנה שכטמן}}) was an Israeli statistician, a [[professor emeritus]] of statistics at the Department of [[Industrial engineering|Industrial Engineering]] and Management, [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]]. She is best known for development (with [[Shlomo Yitzhaki (economist)|Shlomo Yitzhaki]]) of statistical tools that utilize the [[Corrado Gini|Gini]] Mean Difference ([[mean absolute difference|GMD]])<ref>{{cite book |last1=Yitzhaki |first1=Shlomo |last2=Schechtman |first2=Edna |title=The Gini Methodology: A Primer on a Statistical Methodology |date=2013 |url = https://books.google.com/books?id=_9lVaJMwmaUC&q=schechtman+and+yitzhaki
 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-1-4614-4720-7 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=More than a Dozen Alternative Ways of Spelling Gini|first=Shlomo|last=Yitzhaki|journal=Economic Inequality|volume=8|year=1998|pages=13–30|url=http://siteresources.worldbank.org/INTDECINEQ/Resources/morethan2002.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite FTP | author=Yitzhaki, Shlomo | title=Gini's Mean Difference: A Superior Measure of Variability for Non-Normal Distributions | year=2003 | volume=61 | pages=285–316 | issue=2 | server=Metron International Journal of Statistics | url-status=dead | url=ftp://metron.sta.uniroma1.it/RePEc/articoli/2003-2-285-316.pdf }}</ref> (also known as the absolute mean difference and [[mean absolute difference]]) as the measure of association.

==Career==
Schechtman completed her PhD in Statistics at [[Ohio State University]] in 1980, under the supervision of Douglas Wolfe, on the topic: "A Nonparametric Test for the Changepoint Problem".<ref>Wolfe, D. A., & Schechtman, E. (1984). Nonparametric statistical procedures for the changepoint problem. Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference, 9(3), 389-396.</ref> In 1996, she joined the Department of Industrial Engineering and Management, [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]], Israel. She served as the President of the [[:he:האיגוד הישראלי לסטטיסטיקה|Israel Statistical Association]] (2009-2011) and was the Head of the Department of Industrial Engineering and Management, [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]] (2012-2015). She also established the Center for Statistical Consulting <ref>{{Cite web | url=http://in.bgu.ac.il/en/osr/Pages/news/Statistics%20Consulting%20Uni.aspx | title=The Research and Development Authority - the Statistics Consulting Unit at Ben-Gurion University}}</ref> at [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]]. She was a visiting associate professor at several academic institutions, among them [[University of Texas]], [[Texas A&M University]], [[New York University]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. She retired from Ben-Gurion University as a Professor Emeritus in 2017.

==Book: The Gini Methodology: A Primer on a Statistical Methodology==
First introduced by [[Corrado Gini]] in 1912 as an alternative measure of variability, the GMD and its variants (such as the Gini coefficient or the concentration ratio) have been in widespread use in the studies of the income distribution. In their book, Prof. Edna Schechtman and Prof. [[Shlomo Yitzhaki (economist)|Shlomo Yitzhaki]] present GMD statistical tools that replace variance with the GMD and its variants. These new GMD based tools are most justified whenever the researcher cannot conveniently assume a normal distribution of variables under study and used common statistical tools as analysis of correlation, [[analysis of variance]]. This makes the GMD and the tools developed by Prof. Edna Schechtman and Prof. [[Shlomo Yitzhaki (economist)|Shlomo Yitzhaki]] of critical importance in the complex research of statisticians, economists, econometricians, and policymakers.

==Personal life==
Schechtman was born in Israel to her parents, Malka and Reuven Ziegler who immigrated from Poland to Israel in 1946 with her brother, [[:he:צבי ציגלר|Zvi Ziegler]]. The family settled in Jerusalem and then moved to Haifa in 1948.<ref>{{cite web |title=Healing Melanoma |url=https://www.technion.ac.il/en/2014/11/healing-melanoma/ |website=Technion – Israel Institute of Technology |date=November 2014 |access-date=2026-03-03}}</ref> She was married to [[Gideon Schechtman]], a Mathematician at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], and was a mother to four children and a grandmother to ten.{{cn|date=December 2020}}
